cita: Tanguturi (2026). ATANT v1.1: Positioning Continuity Evaluation Against Memory, Long-Context, and Agentic-Memory Benchmarks.
problema: Argues the field conflates 'continuity' (persistence across session termination, update handling, temporal ordering, disambiguation, reconstruction, model independence, operational usefulness) with what popular memory/long-context benchmarks actually measure, leaving update-handling, reconstruction and model-independence essentially untested by any prior benchmark.
mecanismo: Not a memory mechanism itself (operaciones/representacion=NA): the paper's method is a structural meta-evaluation - for 7 existing benchmarks (LOCOMO, LongMemEval, BEAM, MemoryBench, Zep eval, MemGPT/Letta, RULER) it inspects each benchmark's scoring function and corpus to assign a x/partial/check rating against ATANT v1.0's 7 continuity properties, producing a 7x7 property-coverage matrix (Table 1).
evaluacion: Ran Kenotic's own ATANT reference implementation on ATANT (96% cumulative-scale, 1761/1835 questions) and on 3 of LOCOMO's 10 conversations (476 items) as a calibration pair; built the 7-benchmark x 7-property coverage matrix from published corpora/runners rather than re-running third-party systems against ATANT.
numeros_clave: Median existing-benchmark coverage 1.0/7, mean 0.43/7, none scores above 2/7; Kenotic's own system scores 8.8% on LOCOMO (42/476) vs 96% on ATANT cumulative-scale, an 87-point divergence taken as calibration evidence the two measure different properties; LOCOMO's empty-gold matcher bug makes ~23% (444/1986) of items unscorable by construction (Table 1, Sec 2.1, Sec 3).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Argues (Sec 2.2) that a large-enough context window passes LongMemEval/BEAM with zero external memory architecture, i.e. measured retrieval accuracy alone cannot certify a memory layer exists without a model-independence control - a caution against over-trusting raw G-M2 benchmark numbers.

Its 'update handling' property (persist both historical and current state through process termination, historical remains queryable as historical) is a concrete staleness/versioning test MF could adopt to check its own docs-as-truth claims (Sec 2.2, property definitions).

notes: Table 1 property-coverage matrix Sec 3, Sec 2.1 LOCOMO matcher-bug artifact, Sec 5 limitations (arXiv:2604.10981v2). RECONSIDERAR - single-author self-published critique evaluating the author's own commercial benchmark/product, no third-party peer reproduction of the ATANT score.

cita: Perera et al. (2026). AgenticAI-DialogGen: Topic-Guided Conversation Generation for Fine-Tuning and Evaluating Short- and Long-Term Memories of LLMs.
problema: Addresses the lack of conversational datasets that jointly encode short- and long-term memory with topic continuity and persona grounding for fine-tuning/evaluating LLM memory, since existing QA datasets lack persona/topic structure and open-domain datasets lack QA/memory grounding.
mecanismo: AgenticAI-DialogGen extracts subject-relation-object knowledge triples from raw conversations, clusters them into topics, builds per-speaker-per-topic knowledge graphs (WRITE of long-term memory), infers persona profiles from those graphs, then simulates topic-guided dialogue turns (short-term memory) via LangGraph agents, validates/refines them, and generates memory-grounded QA pairs drawn from both the knowledge graph (long-term) and the simulated conversation (short-term).
evaluacion: Human evaluation (4 NLP annotators, 10% sample) compared TGC vs MSC on topic consistency/factual correctness/completeness/coherence/naturalness plus knowledge-graph and QA quality; automatic evaluation (BERTScore, Self-BLEU, perplexity, ROUGE, semantic similarity, entity overlap, Flesch readability) across MSC/PersonaChat/DailyDialog source datasets with an ablation comparing validated vs unvalidated generation; downstream fine-tuning of lightweight LLMs on TGC evaluated on memory-grounded QA.
numeros_clave: TGC vs MSC human eval: topic consistency +33.7pts (97.82% vs 64.12%), completeness +22.9pts (88.22% vs 65.31%), coherence +7.5pts; knowledge-graph factual correctness 92.18%, QA factual correctness 86.82%; ablation TGC-with-validation BERTScore-F1 30.36 vs without-validation 24.70 vs source MSC 12.44 (Table 3-4).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Produces a synthetic dataset/benchmark rather than a deployable memory system, so it bears on MF only as training/eval-data infrastructure, not directly on context-economy at inference time (Sec 4).

Every extracted knowledge triple retains a reference to its originating conversational turn index (Sec 3.2), a lightweight per-fact provenance pattern MF could reuse to ground derived facts back to a source doc.

notes: Table 1-4, Sec 5.1-5.2 human+automatic eval (arXiv:2604.12179v1); a dataset-generation paper, not a deployed memory system, relevant mainly as training/eval infra rather than architecture.

cita: Zheng et al. (2026). To Know is to Construct: Schema-Constrained Generation for Agent Memory.
problema: Targets 'structural hallucination' in generative agent memory (LLM generates memory keys that don't exist, causing lookup failures) and the semantic gap in dense retrieval (embeddings conflate semantically-similar but contextually-distinct entries).
mecanismo: SCG-MEM stores memory as a dynamic Cognitive Schema (Prefix Trie of valid concept keys) constructed via constrained-decoding assimilation (ADMISION: grounding new turns into existing schema nodes) or free-generation accommodation (ACTUALIZACION: expanding the Trie with novel concepts when perplexity is high); recall is schema-constrained beam-search decoding that provably only emits valid keys, followed by activation propagation over a co-occurrence-weighted Associative Graph to gather multi-hop context, mapped back to source text.
evaluacion: Evaluated on LoCoMo (avg 9K-token, up to 35-session dialogues) across Single-Hop, Multi-Hop, Temporal and Adversarial categories with F1/BLEU-1, on Qwen2.5 (1.5B/3B) and Llama 3.2 (1B/3B), against LoCoMo full-context, ReadAgent, MemoryBank, MemGPT and A-MEM baselines, plus an ablation removing the schema constraint and the evolutionary (assimilation) update.
numeros_clave: SCG-Mem beats strongest baseline A-MEM across all categories/models, e.g. +146.7% F1 Single-Hop and +126.6% F1 Multi-Hop on Qwen2.5 3B (Table 1); ablation: removing the schema constraint drops Multi-Hop F1 by -39.5%, removing the evolutionary/assimilation update drops it by -34.2% (Table 2).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Measures that pure dense retrieval underperforms schema-constrained generation by a wide margin on LoCoMo (e.g. +146.7% F1 vs A-MEM, Table 1), challenging any assumption that vector-similarity search alone is a sufficient measured retrieval layer.

The hard-constraint guarantee that a generated key is always a valid schema member (Eq. 2) is a formal anti-hallucination mechanism for memory access (never point to a non-existent fact), a pattern MF could adopt against poisoning by a fabricated reference.

cita: Mao et al. (2026). What Happens Inside Agent Memory? Circuit Analysis from Emergence to Diagnosis.
problema: Agent-memory failures are silent (fluent output even when extraction/retrieval fails) and the write-manage-read loop's external behavior conflates which internal stage (extraction, routing/management, or read grounding) actually failed, so there is no way to localize a wrong answer to a specific memory operation.
mecanismo: Traces feature circuits (pretrained linear transcoders + attribution graphs) through each memory-pipeline stage (Write=extract facts, Manage=add/update/delete/none, Read=answer from retrieved memory) across the Qwen-3 family (0.6B-14B) and two frameworks (mem0, A-MEM); finds routing (Manage) circuitry is causal from 0.6B while content circuits (Write/Read) emerge only at 4B and converge on a shared late-layer 'hub' recruited (not newly built) from the base model's generic context-grounding substrate; turns the discovered feature-space separation between operations into an unsupervised, per-operation failure-localization diagnostic.
evaluacion: Circuits traced and causally verified (zero-ablation vs. matched-random-feature ablation, bootstrapped 95% CIs) on 200 attribution graphs per operation per scale on LongMemEval (500 questions, 5 memory types); cross-system replication on A-MEM; steerability tested via amplification sweeps (2x-10x) measuring fact recall/QA accuracy; the resulting unsupervised diagnostic is benchmarked against majority-class, output-entropy, behavioral-rule and trained logistic-regression baselines, and generalized zero-shot to two more benchmarks (LoCoMo, MAB).
numeros_clave: Manage circuit is causal at 0.6B (causal gap 0.259) while Write/Read show no signal until 4B; Write-Manage Jaccard drops to 0 at 14B while Write-Read stays positive; the unsupervised stage-diagnostic reaches 76.2% localization accuracy at 8B, beating the best trained baseline (logistic regression, 63.4%) by 13 points and generalizing to LoCoMo (68.3%) and MAB (72.5%) without retraining (Tables 2-5, Fig 3-6).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Delivers a concrete, unsupervised diagnostic that localizes WHICH memory operation (write/manage/read) silently failed at 76.2% accuracy without retraining (Table 4-5), a reusable pattern MF could adapt to attribute a drift/poisoning incident to a specific pipeline stage.

Its causal-verification methodology (ablation vs matched-random-feature baseline, bootstrap CIs) is a rigorous measurement discipline consistent with MF's measured-retrieval stance, but the object measured is internal model circuitry, not an external retrieval-quality metric (Sec 3.2).

notes: Table 2-5, Fig 3-7, Sec 4.4 hub analysis (arXiv:2605.03354v2, mechanistic-interpretability venue); dense/technical, digested at synthesis level.

cita: Liao et al. (2026). Belief Memory: Agent Memory Under Partial Observability.
problema: Targets 'self-reinforcing error' in agent memory: existing methods collapse each noisy observation to a single deterministic conclusion (e.g. 'API X failed'), discarding competing hypotheses so the agent never revisits and reinforces an initially wrong conclusion over time, framed as agents operating under partial observability (POMDP) but treating each observation as ground truth.
mecanismo: BeliefMem WRITEs each attribute as a set of candidate-hypothesis probabilities rather than one conclusion; Add initializes a new attribute's supported candidates, Merge (ACTUALIZACION) updates existing candidate probabilities via a noisy-OR evidence merge as new observations arrive (competing candidates get down-weighted), and retrieval scores entries by semantic similarity times temporal decay, returning the full belief distribution over candidates (not just the top pick) so the agent can act on high-confidence knowledge while still seeing alternatives.
evaluacion: Evaluated on LoCoMo (long-term conversation, F1/BLEU-1 across single-hop/multi-hop/temporal/open-domain, GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini backbones) and ALFWorld (embodied, seen/unseen splits, success rate + steps, Qwen3-Next-80B backbone) against LoCoMo-baseline, ReadAgent, MemoryBank, MemGPT, A-MEM, Mem0, LangMem, MemoryOS and a No-Memory control, plus ablation/adversarial experiments on belief preservation.
numeros_clave: LoCoMo (GPT-4o): BeliefMem average F1/BLEU 42.87/37.08 vs best baseline Mem0 39.66/29.54, with the largest gain on Temporal (50.81 vs 44.55 F1); ALFWorld: BeliefMem beats 2nd-best ReadAgent by 11% success rate overall and by 12.4% on the unseen split, while using only half the memory corpus (Table 1-2).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Directly targets the fidelity failure mode of collapsing an ambiguous observation into one stored conclusion (self-reinforcing error, Fig 1/Sec 3.2); its noisy-OR belief-update is a concrete alternative to point-estimate writes MF could weigh when a fact is genuinely uncertain at write time.

Measured gains concentrate on multi-hop/temporal-reasoning tasks that require reconciling conflicting evidence (Table 1), reinforcing that retrieval quality on ambiguous facts should be measured per-task rather than assumed uniform.

notes: Table 1-2 LoCoMo/ALFWorld results, Sec 3.2-3.3 belief-update math (arXiv:2605.05583v2).

cita: Liao et al. (2026). MemQ: Integrating Q-Learning into Self-Evolving Memory Agents over Provenance DAGs.
problema: Targets a credit-assignment gap in self-evolving episodic memory: existing RL-based retrieval-value methods update each memory's value from single-step outcomes in isolation, so a memory that only indirectly enabled a later success (via a chain of retrieved-then-created memories) never receives credit and its value stagnates.
mecanismo: MemQ records a provenance DAG (WRITE) linking each newly built memory to the set of memories retrieved to produce it; it formalizes retrieval as an Exogenous-Context MDP and propagates TD(lambda) eligibility traces backward through the DAG, updating (ACTUALIZACION) every ancestor memory's Q-value with credit weight decaying as (gamma*lambda)^d in DAG depth d rather than temporal distance; retrieval combines a locality (embedding-similarity) filter with epsilon-greedy Q-guided top-k selection.
evaluacion: Evaluated on six benchmarks (LifeLongAgentBench OS interaction, BFCL v3 function calling, LiveCodeBench v6 coding, MMMU Pro multimodal, ERQA embodied reasoning, GPQA Diamond expert QA) on held-out generalization and runtime-learning splits against No-Memory, RAG, Self-RAG, Mem0, MemP and MemRL (single-step EMA) baselines, plus ablations on the discount factor gamma and trace decay lambda.
numeros_clave: MemQ attains the highest success rate on all six benchmarks in runtime learning and five of six in held-out generalization (e.g. LLAB 74.67% vs best baseline MemRL 74.44%); gains are largest on multi-step tasks with deep provenance chains (up to +5.7pp) and smallest on single-step classification (+0.77pp) (Table 1, Abstract).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Directly measures retrieval-value learning against fixed-heuristic and single-step-EMA baselines across 6 benchmarks (Table 1), the kind of per-mechanism measured comparison MF's G-M2 requires rather than assuming any one retrieval scoring is best.

The provenance DAG that records which memories caused a later memory to be built, with credit propagated back proportionally to structural depth, is a concrete mechanism for identifying which past memories should be promoted/reinforced (durable) vs left low-value, relevant to MF's consolidation anchor (Sec 3-4).

notes: Table 1, Sec 3-4 EC-MDP and provenance-DAG mechanics (arXiv:2605.08374v3).
